# Forum digest: "A few statement rows get the wrong category or payee"

Collected from a user support thread. In every case the money moved correctly;
only the derived label is wrong - the category, the sub-tag, or the counterparty
name - and only on a handful of unusual row shapes. Three representative posts,
lightly anonymized, then a maintainer note.

---

**mango_saver** -
> Two rows on this month's statement look off. A credit whose reference note is
> nothing but a long all-numeric string used to show up as a cheque deposit and
> now it just reads as a generic transfer. Separately, my salary credit - whose
> narration is a bare numeric code and nothing else - has stopped picking up the
> salary sub-tag it always had.

**rk_ontheroad** -
> Mine is the name field, not the category. On transfers whose narration opens
> with a direction word ahead of the name, the counterparty now comes back
> empty or wrong. Ordinary transfers that don't open that way are still
> labelled fine; it's only that leading-keyword narration style.

**auditlens** -
> Bill transfers that use a slash-delimited reference are pulling the wrong
> payee. When the reference is laid out as four fields - a type, a sub-type, a
> numeric reference, then the payee name as the final field - the app is lifting
> the numeric reference into the name column instead of the actual name sitting
> at the end.

---

**Maintainer note.** Consolidating these. Each one sits on an edge form that
everyday rows rarely produce, which is why routine activity looks healthy and
nothing tripped in review. On top of the three above we reproduced one more in
the same family: an offsetting credit that arrives immediately after its
matching debit is being recorded as a bounce rather than the reversal it
really is.

The labeling logic is deterministic - the same row always maps to the same
label - so each complaint can be recreated from a single synthetic row and
chased to the exact rule at fault. Expect the faults to sit on boundaries and
structural offsets inside otherwise-correct rules, not in the common paths.

**Ask for engineering:** restore correct handling so these edge rows label
correctly again, without shifting any row that already comes out right. Success
is that the situations described here enrich correctly and nothing that is
currently correct changes.
I'll start by exploring the codebase to understand the transaction enrichment logic.

### Build / run tooling

### Tests: **there are none**
- No `tests/`, no `test_*.py`, no `conftest.py`, no `pytest.ini`/`setup.cfg`/`pyproject.toml`/`tox.ini`/`Makefile`/CI config anywhere (verified by exhaustive `find`).

- Only "test" traces are commented-out matplotlib dendrogram debug blocks: `SalaryDetection.py:27-32` and `RecurrentTxns.py:16-21` (both labelled "For testing purpose only").
- Git history is a single commit `0a1b6a3 "import codebase"` (54 files, 11 242 insertions) — no test files ever existed.
- All modules compile cleanly: `python3 -m py_compile UtilityScripts/*.py BankScripts/*.py Controller.py __init__.py` → exit 0.
- **How you would run tests if added**: `pip install -e categorizationapp` then `pytest`. ### Pipeline / data contract (important for writing tests)
`Controller.py:69-936` — `POST /categorizeTransaction` with payload `{bank, acc_type, accountUID, accountHolder, isPFMEnabled, transactions[]}`; `POST /recurrentTransactions` (`Controller.py:55-67`); `GET /` (`Controller.py:51-53`).

Order of enrichment (repeated verbatim per bank, e.g. `Controller.py:91-114` for ANDHRA_BANK):
1. `AppUtil.clean_input_df` (`Controller.py:87`; `AppUtil.py:6-12`) — strips `description`, numeric-casts `amount` & `balanceAfterTransaction`.
2. `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType)` → sets **`transactionCategory`** (default `"TRANSFER"`), then **`transactionSubcategory`**, **`merchantType`**, **`partyName`**, **`party2`**.
3. If `CREDIT_CARD`: `card_clean_names` → `card_purpose`.
4. `purpose(transactions, accountType)` — subcategory + merchantType.
5. `clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)` — canonical payee names.
6. `internal_payment(...)` if `accountHolder` non-empty.
7. `salary_detection(...)` if `accountType == "SAVING"` (falls back to un-mutated frame if it returns `None`).
8. If `isPFMEnabled`: `pfm_categorization` → `simple_description`.
9. Response: `transactions.to_json(orient='records')`.

Input columns consumed: `description` (6109 refs), `type` ("DEBIT"/"CREDIT"), `amount`, `remark`, `transactionDate` (`%d/%m/%Y`, `SalaryDetection.py:56`), `balanceAfterTransaction`. Derived columns: `transactionCategory`, `transactionSubcategory`, `merchantType`, `partyName`, `party2` (partyName with spaces removed), `isInternalPayment`, `Group_ID`, `pfmCategoryOne/Two/Type`, `pfmSimpleDescription`.

Rule idiom used everywhere: a list of `[boolean-Series, value]` pairs → `pd.DataFrame(...,columns=['conditions','choices'])` → `np.select(...)`. **First matching rule wins**, so ordering within each list is semantically significant.

    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    for col in ("remark",):

    if "balanceAfterTransaction" not in df:
        df["balanceAfterTransaction"] = 1000.0

steps.message:
Traced all five reported symptoms to five one-token faults, each on a boundary or structural offset inside an otherwise-correct rule.

## Fixes

**`BankScripts/HDFC.py:100`** — cheque deposit from all-numeric reference
`remark.str.len().eq(15)` combined with `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` (16 characters) was unsatisfiable, so those credits fell through to the default `TRANSFER`. HDFC remarks are 16 chars everywhere else in the file (lines 214-215: `^N[0-9]{15}$`, `^[0-9]{16}$`), so the length check is now `.eq(16)`.

**`BankScripts/HDFC.py:124`** — salary sub-tag on bare numeric narration
Guard compared `accountType == "SAVINGS"`; the canonical enum value passed by `Controller.py` and used by every other script is `"SAVING"`, so the rule never fired.

**`BankScripts/ICICI.py:159`** — counterparty on direction-keyword narrations
`py_extract(..., pat="TRFR (TO|FROM):(.*)", index=0)` returned capture group 1 — the direction word itself. `"To"` was then blanked by the 1-2 letter cleanup at line 233 (empty name) and `"From"` survived verbatim (wrong name). Now `index=1`, the name group. Matches the sibling idiom at `DCB.py:80-81`.

**`BankScripts/ICICI.py:147`** — slash-delimited bill reference
For `^BIL/INFT/` with exactly 3 slashes (`BIL / INFT / <numeric ref> / <payee>`), the rule lifted field index 2 (the numeric ref) instead of the final field. Now `sep_by_(description, 3, 4)`, consistent with the 5-field variant at line 154.

**`BankScripts/HDFC.py:98`** — reversal vs. bounce
The reversal branch compared `description.eq(description.shift(2))` while the pair it describes is adjacent, so it never matched and the offsetting credit fell to the `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE` branch below. Now `shift(1)`, identical to the unaffected reference implementation at `ICICI.py:49-50`.

## Verification

No test suite exists in this repo, so I validated with synthetic rows through the full pipeline (`clean_input_df` → bank script → `purpose` → `clean_names` → `salary_detection`) and diffed a ~68-row corpus of common HDFC/ICICI narrations (UPI, IMPS, NEFT/RTGS, POS, ATM, ACH/SI, cheque, cash, interest, FD/RD) against `HEAD` for both `SAVING` and `CURRENT`.

The only rows that changed are the five reported ones: `TRANSFER`→`CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`, empty→`SALARY`, empty/`From`→`Ramesh Kumar`/`Sunita Sharma`, empty→`Rajesh Traders`, `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`→`REVERSAL`. Genuine autopay bounces (`ACH D-` pairs) still classify as `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`, and the 5-field `BIL/INFT` variant is untouched.
